chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated, from ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAlī ibn al-Sindī, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Shuʿayb, from Abī Baṣīr, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who finds semen on his garment and does not know that he had a nocturnal emission. He said: Let him wash what he found on his garment and perform wudu (ablution).

This report does not contradict the first two reports, because the way to reconcile them is that the garment which no one else shares with him in using it—whenever he finds semen on it, ghusl (ritual bath) and repeating the salat (prayer) are obligatory upon him if he had already prayed, since it is possible that he had forgotten the nocturnal emission. But as for what someone else shares with him in using, it does not make ghusl obligatory upon him unless he becomes certain of the nocturnal emission.

key_terms.احْتَلَمَ: to have experienced a nocturnal emission
key_terms.الْغُسْلُ: the ritual bath required in janabah
key_terms.لِيَغْسِلْ: he should wash the affected area

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone finds semen on his garment but does not remember having a nocturnal emission?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the legal ruling concerning a person who finds semen on his garment without remembering a nocturnal emission. The reconciliation given distinguishes between a garment exclusively used by the person and one shared with others, affecting whether ghusl and repetition of salat (prayer) become obligatory.
